evidence: Ordering is as described: process_pull_request_event (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:810, @shared_task max_retries=3, default_retry_delay=5) runs _inbox_rereview_carve_out inside its own try/retry (tasks.py:870-879) BEFORE the head-changing skip path's retraction (tasks.py:888-903: _resolve_repo_config + _retract_stale_approvals_on_skip), and _mark_pr_event_processed only runs after that (tasks.py:911). Celery 5.6.3 Task.retry re-raises the passed exc once request.retries > max_retries, so an exhausted carve-out retry ends the task with the retraction never attempted; the webhook already returned 202 (products/stamphog/backend/presentation/webhooks.py:61-64) and nothing reconciles later (the only crontab is the daily digest, products/stamphog/backend/tasks/schedules.py:13; approvals.py:24-70 is invoked only from the workflow activity and this task). The carve-out adds new dependencies in front of that safety step: for a bot-authored repo-native PR it passes the cheap early-outs (tasks.py:169, 177) and then reads the stamphog product DB (tasks.py:179) plus the DEFAULT DB via find_signal_implementation_run (tasks.py:191 -> products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:504 -> products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:41 TaskRun, a plain models.Model at products/tasks/backend/models.py:1063) and the registered review_hog resolver (tasks.py:201-205 -> products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:151-156: SignalReportArtefact at receivers.py:181, Team/OrganizationMembership/UserSocialAuth/User via products/signals/backend/report_generation/resolve_reviewers.py:314-349, ReviewUserSettings.load at receivers.py:154). The retraction itself needs only the stamphog DB (ProductTeamModel, models.py:24/78/140, routed by ProductDBRouter, posthog/settings/data_stores.py:262; distinct aliases stamphog_db_writer/reader per products/stamphog/backend/tests/conftest.py:32) and GitHub (logic/approvals.py:45-70). So a default-DB (or signals resolver) failure lasting longer than the ~20s retry window on a synchronize/reopened for a self-driving PR leaves the receiver-leg approval at the old head standing, with no later event guaranteed to retract it: a subsequent ready_for_review is not in _HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS (tasks.py:50) and the carve-out returns early for it (tasks.py:167), so the stale approval survives until some later push. Human PRs are unaffected (carve-out returns at tasks.py:169 with no DB work), and other bot PRs have no PullRequest row so the retraction is a no-op for them anyway (tasks.py:503-506); the affected class is exactly the PRs that carry receiver-leg approvals. The module's own decision record says dismissal must never be preference-gated (tests/test_tasks.py:762-795), yet it is now availability-gated on a second database. No test exercises a carve-out exception (zero hits for stamphog_pr_event_inbox_carve_out_failed in tests/test_tasks.py). Not must_fix: the trigger is an infrastructure outage coinciding with a push, not an attacker-reachable input, and the identical retry-exhaust-then-drop shape already exists for the product-DB/GitHub dependencies (tasks.py:855-863, 888-903, 917-921), so the 'durable reconciliation' half of the suggestion is pre-existing design rather than a regression of this PR. The reorder half is a cheap, correct fix: retract at tasks.py:888 before calling the carve-out (dismiss_stale_approvals_for_head is idempotent via approval_dismissed_at, approvals.py:36-39, so a following re-review's workflow dismissal stays a no-op); only the opt-out message choice (tasks.py:897) depends on the carve-out result.
notes: Would downgrade to consider if stamphog and tasks/signals/review_hog were pinned to the same Postgres instance in production (then a default-DB outage fails the retraction too and the ordering adds nothing), or if the carve-out's final retry attempt fell through to the retraction instead of re-raising. Would upgrade to must_fix if any carve-out failure were deterministic (e.g. a resolver exception for a specific report shape) since that would block retraction for every push to that PR, or if a caller could trigger the exception.
